items.headline: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
items.blurb: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
items.text: The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy. The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions. The move follows the White House's investigation into the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal . China is facing the highest rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35% and then others facing either 20% or 25%. The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year. Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of the good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing the products from abroad. Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies. items.headline: Man United denied at Sporting as referee overshadows Fernandes double
items.blurb: Bruno Fernandes nets twice in Lisbon, but referee's decisions in spotlight as Mauricio Pochettino denied first win.
items.text: Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach, after a wild 2–2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side. United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half. Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game. United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match. A crushing 4–0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick. items.headline: At least 30 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
items.blurb: Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 25 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said.
items.text: Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 25 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the public prosecutor’s office said in a statement. The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the health ministry. At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb. The Egyptian president, Abdel-Fattah al-Sissi , expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. items.headline: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
items.blurb: The asteroid's surface was transformed after a spacecraft was deliberately crashed into it four years ago
items.text: The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface. The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision. "The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team. "It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful." The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h). items.headline: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
items.blurb: About 200,000 tents need replacing, Gaza’s municipalities say, as the EU urges Israel to reopen all crossings.
items.text: Gaza’s municipalities have warned that winter rains could flood about 1,000 camps and other sites hosting displaced Palestinians in the war-torn enclave, adding that damage to drains and sewers, and a shortage of pumps, have left their crews with little means to clear the water. After a meeting in Gaza City on Wednesday, the Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities singled out al-Mughraqa and al-Zahra in central Gaza, where water levels in Wadi Gaza could rise suddenly. Across the territory, about 200,000 tents need replacing, and more than 2,000 damaged buildings are at risk of collapse, the union said. Gaza’s Government Media Office had warned on Tuesday that it expected another storm within days. This is Gaza’s fourth winter since Israel launched its war in October 2023. The union said storms in early November flooded about 70,000 tents and affected more than 350,000 displaced people. During a winter storm this November, families piled sand at tent entrances to keep out the rain. Others carried their children out and salvaged what belongings they could. items.blurb: Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.
items.text: Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon . The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports. The elephants attacked the group and Alain Throo, a Swiss insurance executive based in London, was reportedly gored and one of the guides tossed into a ditch on top of Throo, while the others hid in trees. items.headline: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
items.blurb: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.
items.text: Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says. Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening. Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched. Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol. The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead. The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation. items.blurb: Virginia schools face scrutiny after revelations of abuse and widespread failures in mandatory staff background checks.
items.text: The United States Department of Education says it is launching an investigation and withholding funding from a district in the state of Virginia after local officials shut down all of its schools in the wake of a child sexual abuse scandal involving its employees. “Parents should never have to question whether their child’s school is aiding and abetting child predators,” US Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said in a statement on Tuesday. “The Trump Administration is taking decisive enforcement action to hold those responsible accountable and ensure Virginia schools are safe places for children to learn.” Officials in Albemarle County, Virginia, announced they were closing all 29 schools in the district last week, after learning that more than 500 staff had not been subjected to a routine background screening for a history of child sexual abuse. The school system has about 2,800 employees, and only a fraction of its $284m budget comes from the federal government. However, the then home secretary, Yvette Cooper, denied Peramalya entry to the UK due to his criminal convictions while he was on Diego Garcia for four counts of sexual assault, one count of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and one count of arson. items.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
items.blurb: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.
items.text: Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival. The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage. They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third. Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately". "Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement. Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war. The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. items.blurb: “The Notice is currently under examination,” the ministry said, adding that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation.
items.text: The government of India on Wednesday said it was examining a notice issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in a probe into manufacturing capacity across 14 economies, including India, and reiterated that the country does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. In a statement issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the government said it had taken note of the notice of determination and request for comments issued by the USTR under Section 301 of the US Trade Act. “The Notice is currently under examination,” the ministry said, adding that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation. The Department of Commerce had stated, in its response to the notice of initiation and subsequent proceedings, that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector, the statement said. items.text: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam. Chandana was speaking at the 45th Vikram Sarabhai Memorial Lecture on "Find Your Space in Space: The Story of a 2026 Spacepreneur – Roots to Wings: From Vikram Sarabhai to Vikram-1, and Beyond". Recalling the vision of India's space programme, he said it was inspired by Dr Vikram Sarabhai, who wanted the country to be second to none in applying advanced technologies for the benefit of the common man. "That started the journey of ISRO and India's space programme," he said. Chandana said the first private rocket launch by Skyroot Aerospace was only a beginning, adding that the seeds sown in India's private space sector would grow into a much larger ecosystem in the future. items.blurb: Some of the accused became acquainted in prison; stolen valuables worth ₹2.39 lakh recovered, four others wanted in the Mumbra case
items.text: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested five members of a gang allegedly involved in targeting bungalows and farmhouses across Thane district, solving eight cases, including the November 17 dacoity in Mumbra, officials said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Police have recovered stolen valuables worth ₹2.39 lakh from the accused. The arrested accused have been identified as Vijay Chavan (45), Laxman Bhosale (43), Satish Waghe (27), Narayan Thombre (27), and Jayesh Kathore (35). All five have been remanded in police custody till November 30, while a search is underway for four other accused directly linked to the Mumbra case. According to the police, eight to nine persons allegedly broke into the bungalow of complainant Tukaram Munde in Mumbra on November 17, threatened him with sharp weapons, restrained him and fled with gold ornaments worth ₹1.55 lakh and ₹84,000 in cash. Police have since recovered the stolen property. items.blurb: The Union Budget for 2027–28 is scheduled for February 1; it will be Nirmala Sitharaman's 10th straight Budget and the fourth of the Modi 3.0 government.
items.text: The finance ministry has imposed restrictions on the entry of media persons into Kartavya Bhavan-1 till the Budget presentation. The restrictions, effective from November 30, have been imposed in view of the commencement of the Union Budget preparation process, which is now gaining momentum, sources said. Media persons will be allowed entry into Kartavya Bhavan 1 during this period only with specific permission from officers authorised for the purpose, they said. The authorities have asked the concerned officials to ensure strict compliance with the entry restrictions, sources said. The Union Budget for FY 2027–28 is scheduled to be presented on February 1. It will be the fourth budget of the Modi 3.0 government and the 10th straight budget for Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, a rare distinction in Indian polity. The Budget 2027–28 would be presented against the backdrop of global supply chain disruptions triggered by the ongoing West Asia crisis and moderation in global growth. items.headline: BNP Paribas moves up global systemic bank list, capital buffer rises
items.blurb: BNP PARIBAS-CAPITAL/:BNP Paribas moves up global systemic bank list, capital buffer rises
items.text: Nov 25 (Reuters) - BNP Paribas moved up on the 2026 list of global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) published each year by the Financial Stability Board. The move increases the capital buffer the French bank is required to hold to 2%, up from 1.5%. The only other bank that shifted on the list from a year ago was MUFG, which moved down, decreasing its capital buffer to 1%, from its current 1.5%. The number of banks on the list remained the same as last year at 29. The annual list has been constant since 2023, when China-based Bank of Communications was added and Credit Suisse and UniCredit were removed. JPMorgan was once again ranked as the most systemically important bank to the global financial system, and the only bank required to meet a capital buffer of 2.5%. Banks in the second-highest bucket of the 2026 list, required to have an additional capital buffer of 2%, include Bank of America, Citigroup, HSBC, ICBC, as well as BNP Paribas. On one side, Andrew Freedman, a communications and software analyst at Hedgeye Risk Management, has put out reports since the company’s initial public offering and said in an interview on Wednesday that the stock is trading at levels that should be attractive for long-term investors. Meanwhile, his colleague Felix Wang, a global tech analyst, sent out a note to clients on Tuesday, recommending they short the stock. items.headline: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
items.blurb: The discount chain has fallen into administration after its owners failed to find a buyer.
items.text: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business. The retailer's shops and distribution centres will remain open and continue to trade during the administration process with the business likely to be broken up and some of its stores sold off to rival retailers. Poundland's US owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal, but no agreement was reached. Poundland boss Barry Williams said in a note to staff that the board had "no alternative but to take this decision", but was making it with "sincere sadness and intense regret". He said the US owners Gordon Brothers had removed "all borrowing facilities and access to our bank accounts" on 27 October, and adequate funds had not been released since then to keep the business solvent. "Under these circumstances, it is impossible for the board of directors to see how Poundland can continue to operate as a going concern," he added. items.blurb: The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s request to launch as many as 1 million satellites for Elon Musk’s vision to build a network of data centers in orbit for complex artificial intelligence computing.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s request to launch as many as 1 million satellites for Elon Musk’s vision to build a network of data centers in orbit for complex artificial intelligence computing. In a statement, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr wrote that the commission was supercharging the US’s ambitions in AI by granting authorization for orbital data centers for the first time. “By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment,” Carr added. The approval clears a regulatory hurdle and brings SpaceX one step closer to its ambitious yet unproven plan for orbital data centers, which the company says can serve as lower-cost and more environmentally friendly alternatives to land-based data centers. Orbital data centers are also key to SpaceX’s future ambitions in AI, which the company pinned its future growth upon during a blockbuster IPO in June. items.text: Zostel has approached the Delhi High Court seeking to revive its claim to a 7% stake in Oravel Stays, OYO's parent company, as it moves towards a proposed IPO. The company has challenged a May 2025 order that set aside a 2021 arbitral award recognising its entitlement to the stake following a proposed acquisition of its hotel aggregation business, Zo Rooms, in 2015. During Wednesday's hearing, Zostel argued that the court should have set aside only the relief granted by the arbitrator rather than the entire award. It maintained that the tribunal's findings on the binding nature of the deal and Oravel's alleged breach should have been retained. The dispute dates back to November 2015, when Oravel and Zostel signed a term sheet for the acquisition of Zo Rooms. Under the proposed deal, Zostel's shareholders were to receive a 7% stake in Oravel. Although the term sheet was described as non-binding, Zostel argued that subsequent actions by both parties made it binding. The final agreements were never signed. items.text: Gurugram-based orthopaedic healthcare startup OSSO has raised Rs 2.5 crore as part of its extended seed funding round. The company will use the fresh capital to expand its clinical capabilities and presence across the National Capital Region (NCR), OSSO said in a press release. The extended round saw participation from Rajeev Saraf, Tejinderpal Miglani, Priyanka Aggarwal, Akshay Varma and Vikas Bhadoria. They join existing investors, including Umesh Kumar Agarwal from the Haldiram Family Office, Sahil Jindal and Blume Founders Fund, among others. Founded in 2025 by Kunal Kishore Dhawan and Avani Shukla, OSSO operates an integrated orthopaedic and rehabilitation centre that combines clinical orthopaedics, physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R), physiotherapy, regenerative orthopaedics and sports injury care. The startup's newly launched centre will focus on advanced orthopaedic procedures, particularly joint preservation and sports injury treatment. The facility will offer procedures such as image-guided orthobiologic interventions, subchondral bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) and arthroscopic cartilage repair. items.headline: AI is straining America’s open records systems
items.blurb: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer.
items.text: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he got rather busy. Panton used to get a request every year or so from a company called SmartProcure for “all purchasing records,” covering everything from road salt to computers to toilet paper. Last year, those requests started coming quarterly. Then different companies began making more specific requests, like records of every purchase related to emergency road flares. These targeted inquiries started coming monthly or more. “I’m happy to answer public records requests from people,” says Rowe, who recently moved into a position at a nearby town. “But answering it for these purposes—it feels like I’m doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers’ time.” Rowe’s experiences are being repeated across the US. While data brokers have mined public records for decades, AI has intensified investors’ interest.

items.headline: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
items.blurb: Frontier AI is already solving problems that once took top physicists a full day.
items.text: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. This thinking isn’t all that fringe. items.headline: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
items.blurb: A new AI-assisted proof seems to be solid, but we're not sure what it tells us.
items.text: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. items.headline: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.blurb: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.text: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang’s affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed’s assurances. Huang’s return doesn’t settle that. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche has suggested Nvidia isn’t a target of an investigation, but California’s attorney general and Congress are pressing ahead, and the Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating, too. The U.S. government opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 and requested information from Nvidia about its billions of dollars in sales to the company, concerned that some of the chips Megaspeed bought for data center projects in Malaysia were in fact being diverted to China. items.text: Sarvam AI has expanded its product portfolio with an upgraded 105B large language model and Dictate, a speech-to-text API supporting English and 22 Indian languages Beyond building sovereign AI models, Sarvam is looking to become a one-stop shop for enterprise AI in India, offering everything from foundation models and inference infrastructure to AI-powered applications While its upgraded 105B model narrows the performance gap with global peers on conversational tasks, its voice AI business is already finding commercial traction, clocking over 3 Mn minutes a day and a billion-plus API calls a month, according to the company Last week, Sarvam AI found itself in the eye of a storm . The poster child of India’s sovereign AI ambitions drew flak for offering access to Chinese AI models, including DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, through its newly launched inference platform, Token Factory. The point of contention among critics has been whether a startup that received government support to build indigenous AI models should be in the business of selling access to Chinese models. items.headline: What Jensen Huang’s NVIDIA Return Means For India’s AI Players
items.blurb: Jensen Huang’s return as NVIDIA CEO has eased concerns over leadership continuity at a key supplier to India’s AI ecosystem.…
items.text: Huang’s return brings greater leadership certainty, but is unlikely to immediately improve GPU availability, lower procurement costs for Indian operators Indian AI companies’ dependence on NVIDIA’s hardware and software leaves them exposed to changes in its supply priorities, global demand, and US export policies NVIDIA accounts for 81.6% of compute units listed on the IndiaAI Compute Portal. Analysts recommend diversifying suppliers, improving infrastructure utilisation Jensen Huang’s return as NVIDIA CEO has eased concerns over leadership continuity at a key supplier to India’s AI ecosystem. However, analysts say it does little to address the Indian AI ecosystem’s dependence on the chipmaker or the constraints keeping advanced computing infrastructure expensive. NVIDIA announced Huang’s reinstatement on November 23, following his resignation on November 12. US President Donald Trump welcomed the decision, describing Huang as a “national treasure”. His departure had raised questions about NVIDIA’s investment plans, supply-chain management, pace of product innovation, and ability to retain talent. items.headline: Update Anthropic Rolls Out Claude Duet In India After US Launch
items.blurb: Update | November 25, 2026, 18:50 IST Anthropic has expanded the research preview of Claude Duet, its AI-powered work assistant,…
items.text: Anthropic has expanded the research preview of Claude Duet, its AI-powered work assistant, to India, a month after its US launch The move brings Anthropic’s proactive AI agent to Indian professionals and businesses, allowing them to automate tasks across connected apps Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Duet can schedule meetings, track invoices, prepare financial forecasts and build dashboards Anthropic has expanded the research preview of Claude Duet, its AI-powered work assistant, to India, a month after its US launch. Built on Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 model, Claude Duet can monitor users’ connected apps, identify tasks needing attention, and work in the background even when users are away from their devices. Its capabilities include scheduling meetings, tracking invoices, preparing financial forecasts, building dashboards, and developing web applications. Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work in the background, including when users switch off their devices.
